children: Saudi Arabia awarded 99 projects worth around 123 billion Saudi riyals ($33 billion) in the first nine months of 2026 as the world’s dominant oil exporter pushed ahead with a landmark scheme to diversify its economy and attract capital.

The projects, with an average monthly value of around $3.6 billion, covered oil and gas, industry, construction, energy, water and other sectors, according to the monthly bulletin of the Saudi contractors authority (SCA).

A breakdown showed nearly half the value of the projects was in May and June, standing at around SAR60 billion while June recorded the highest number of awarded public projects of 25, the report showed.

In September, nine projects with a combined value of around SAR7.7 billion were awarded and Acwa emerged as the largest beneficiary, according to the monthly bulletin, which covered project activity in September.

“Acwa had the lion’s share of the public contracts awarded in September in terms of the number of projects and value,” the report said, adding that the company was awarded four projects worth about SAR 3 billion.

Eight projects were expected by SCA to be awarded this month and nearly half of them are in construction. Most of the projects are owned by the state-controlled Saudi Aramco, the transport ministry and the public investment fund.

Saudi Arabia, which controls the world’s second largest extractable oil deposits, has awarded hundreds of projects, including mega works, since it launched the historic Vision 2030 for economic transformation in 2016.
In 2024, the value of the 314 projects awarded by the Kingdom was the highest since the 2020 Covid pandemic, peaking at SAR 268 billion, according to the SCA.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: Saudi Arabia awards $33bln projects in 9 months
